reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read the 'little son' of Genesis 9:24 as comparative rather than superlative, making the standard list order itself reflect relative age.

discrepancy.note: Colenso notes the invariable Shem-Ham-Japheth order implies Shem was eldest, clashing with Genesis 9:24 calling Ham the younger son.

quotes.text: the order is Shem, Ham, Japheth, which is merely reversed in the table of x.2-32, — in order to bring Shem into close connection with the following narrative : whereas in Lx.24 Ham is spoken of as the 'younger' — i.e. youngest — son of Noah… he was plainly regarded as the eldest, and so the order supposed by this writer was 'Shem, Japheth, Ham,'
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. V (1865), on Genesis 9:24.

sides.snippet: Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
sides.verseText: Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

sides.snippet: Noah awoke from his wine, and knew what his youngest son had done to him.
